atoms.text:
Text 1: Easter Island is located in the Pacific Ocean more than 2,200 miles from Chile. It is one of the most remote islands on Earth that is still inhabited. Easter Island has a triangular shape and is formed from three dormant volcanoes. Scientists estimate that the island was first populated by the Rapa Nui people more than 3,000 years ago, and to this day, the island is home to their descendants. Easter Island is world-famous for its more than 900 stone statues that were erected across the whole island.

The traditional name for the statues is moai which loosely translates to stone statue. Most of the moai are more than 500 years old and have been carved out of soft volcanic stone by the Rapa Nui people. Each one of the statues was carved from a single block of stone and then moved across the island to its final destination. Scientists believe that the statues were built to honour and represent deified ancestors or other important people of the island. To this day, it is unclear how the Rapa Nui people moved these massive statues across the island. However, traditional stories, passed down through generations of the Rapa Nui people, claim that the statues 'walked' to their chosen destination. The moai are very holy and powerful stone statues and a symbol of the highly developed culture of the Rapa Nui people.

hint.text:
A dormant volcano is a volcano that is currently not active but is likely to erupt in the future again.
Deified means to make someone or something god-like.

atoms.text:
Text 2: Hoa Hakananai'a is the only moai that is not on Easter Island anymore. In order to find out why that is, we have to go back in time. The British ship Topaze, under the command of Commandore Powell, arrived at Rapa Nui island in 1868. At that time, Britain occupied many parts of the world, increasing their power over other peoples and lands.

After discovering the island and its treasures, the crew wanted to bring back something beautiful to show their homeland. Upon seeing the moai, it was clear what that treasure would be. Eventually, they stumbled upon Hoa Hakananai'a standing upright in the back of a building. The statue was buried to its shoulders. The crew dug the statue out, hoisted it onboard the Topaze and shipped it to Britain. Today, Hoa Hakananai'a stands in the British Museum in London among many other objects.

On that note, it is important to remember that while some objects in the British Museum were gifted to Britain by indigenous peoples from across the world, many others were simply taken and relocated to Britain without their consent. Many of these removed objects are exhibited to this day.

Hoa Hakananai'a can be translated as 'stolen or hidden friend'. This name makes sense, since it is the only moai that is not on Easter Island anymore.

atoms.a: What was the main difference between the two texts?

b.sound: The first text was about Easter Island and the moai in general, while the second text was about one specific moai — namely Hoa Hakananai'a.
The first text was about the Rapa Nui people and the second text was only about people from Britain.

feedback.correct: Correct, scientists estimate that the island was populated by the Rapa Nui people more than 3,000 years ago.

((Another mystery is how the famous Hoa Hakananai'a got to London.)) It_is_the_only_moai_that_is_not_on_Easter_Island_anymore. Instead,_it_is_exhibited_in_the_British_Museum_in_London.

feedback.correct: Correct. It is commonly known that Commodore Powell and his crew shipped Hoa Hakananai'a to Britain.

atoms.a: What is the connection of Hoa Hakananai'a to Easter Island?

b.sound: Hoa Hakananai'a, was originally on Easter Island before he was shipped to Britain.
Easter Island’s original name was Hoa Hakananai'a.

atoms.a: What is problematic about some objects exhibited in the British Museum?

b.sound: Many objects have been taken to Britain without the consent of native peoples.
The British Museum is selling all artifacts that are too old.

atoms.a: Why did the Rapa Nui people build so many moai?

b.sound: The statues were built to honor and represent deified ancestors or other important people of the island.
The moai were supposed to defend the islanders from enemies.
